name: Limited liability and ownership
objective: Explain and apply limited liability and ownership.
explanation: A corporation is legally distinct from its owners. Shareholder losses are generally limited to the investment, while ownership transfer and access to capital differ between private and public corporations.
why: The share investment may be lost. Creditors retain claims on corporate assets; limited liability separates ordinary shareholder personal exposure.
definition: A corporation is legally distinct from its owners.
example: A fully paid shareholder can lose the entire share investment without ordinarily owing the company’s unpaid trade debts personally.
trap: Limited liability does not protect the value of the investment.
mnemonic: Limited liability and ownership → Limited liability does not protect the value of the investment.
recall: Without looking: explain limited liability and ownership and one mistake to avoid.
recallAnswer: A corporation is legally distinct from its owners. Shareholder losses are generally limited to the investment, while ownership transfer and access to capital differ between private and public corporations. Watch for: Limited liability does not protect the value of the investment.

name: Debt holders versus equity holders
objective: Explain and apply debt holders versus equity holders.
explanation: Lenders have contractual claims, while shareholders hold residual claims. Shareholders may favor risky projects with upside even when the additional downside harms lenders.
why: Fixed debt claims capture limited upside but bear larger default losses. Residual equity can gain from increased volatility.
definition: Lenders have contractual claims, while shareholders hold residual claims.

trap: A project favored by shareholders need not improve creditor value.
mnemonic: Debt holders versus equity holders → A project favored by shareholders need not improve creditor value.
recall: Without looking: explain debt holders versus equity holders and one mistake to avoid.
recallAnswer: Lenders have contractual claims, while shareholders hold residual claims. Shareholders may favor risky projects with upside even when the additional downside harms lenders. Watch for: A project favored by shareholders need not improve creditor value.

name: Cash conversion cycle
objective: Explain and apply cash conversion cycle.
explanation: The cash conversion cycle estimates the time between paying suppliers and collecting cash from customers. It combines inventory days and receivable days, then subtracts payable days.
why: 50 + 30 − 40 = 40 days. Supplier credit finances part of the operating cycle.
definition: The cash conversion cycle estimates the time between paying suppliers and collecting cash from customers.
example: Inventory days 50 + receivable days 30 − payable days 40 = 40 days of cash tied up.
trap: Payables reduce the cycle; they are not added.
mnemonic: Cash conversion cycle → Payables reduce the cycle; they are not added.
recall: Without looking: explain cash conversion cycle and one mistake to avoid.
recallAnswer: The cash conversion cycle estimates the time between paying suppliers and collecting cash from customers. It combines inventory days and receivable days, then subtracts payable days. Watch for: Payables reduce the cycle; they are not added.

name: Net present value and relevant cash flows
objective: Explain and apply net present value and relevant cash flows.
explanation: NPV discounts incremental after-tax cash flows at an appropriate required return and subtracts the investment. Sunk costs are excluded; opportunity costs and effects on existing business matter.
why: Discount 121 for two periods to 100, then subtract 100. Undiscounted profit is not NPV.
definition: NPV discounts incremental after-tax cash flows at an appropriate required return and subtracts the investment.
example: Pay 100 now to receive 121 in two years at 10%: NPV = 121/1.1² − 100 = 0.
trap: Past research spending is sunk, not a new incremental project outflow.
mnemonic: Net present value and relevant cash flows → Past research spending is sunk, not a new incremental project outflow.
recall: Without looking: explain net present value and relevant cash flows and one mistake to avoid.
recallAnswer: NPV discounts incremental after-tax cash flows at an appropriate required return and subtracts the investment. Sunk costs are excluded; opportunity costs and effects on existing business matter. Watch for: Past research spending is sunk, not a new incremental project outflow.
